newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: QAF rises after Salim's asset injection.
newsitem.headline: QAF rises after Salim's asset injection.

text.p: QAF Ltd shares rose on Wednesday morning after its Indonesian major shareholder said it would inject PT Indofood Sukses Makmur into the bread manufacturer.
At 0200 GMT, QAF shares were trading around Singapore $1.84, up four cents after hitting a high of S$1.88. Volume was over 1.7 million shares
Brokers said the shares were given a boost after the Salim Group, which owns 70 percent of QAF, said it would buy a majority stake in Indofood, the world's biggest instant noodle maker.
The move will cost QAF and estimated QAF S$2.75 billion in cash. It plans to raise S$2.2 billion through a massive rights issue and the rest from bank borrowings.

Brokers said the gains in QAF shares were capped by concerns over the huge amount of money the company will have to raise to complete the deal, which amounts to the biggest takeover in Singapore corporate history.
"The financing is large despite the fact the move will be good for QAF as it will diversify its earnings base from a mere bread making company," said an analyst with a European brokerage.
